subject.title: Improve context overflow error message with specifics

question: Which context-overflow facts should OpenClaw show to end users instead of keeping only in logs or session metadata?
rationale: Current code already has token, model, route, and session facts, but exposing raw session keys/channel identifiers and exact token counts changes privacy, support, and cross-channel UX policy that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Show redacted diagnostics
options.body: Expose provider/model, effective context budget, estimated or observed token count, overage, and a redacted channel/session label while keeping raw identifiers in logs.

options.title: Keep specifics operator-only
options.body: Leave chat copy generic and document logs or status metadata as the supported way to inspect context-pressure facts.

options.title: Defer to broader context visibility
options.body: Keep this issue open until a broader design decides shared UI, logs, and channel-message context telemetry together.

recommendation.title: Show redacted diagnostics
recommendation.body: Expose provider/model, effective context budget, estimated or observed token count, overage, and a redacted channel/session label while keeping raw identifiers in logs.
